column1: # Luxel partition table for 16 MB flash (Gitea #501). Same shape as
# partitions.csv — no factory partition
# with every region scaled to the bigger part: 3 MiB (0x300000) app slots
# 4 MiB (0x400000) storage for the device pattern library
# (0x3F0000) assets partition for the packed playground.
# ONLY board-seengreat-hub75 uses this table. That board is the one piece of
# Luxel hardware whose module is known to carry 16 MB — an
# ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 (16 MB flash + 8 MB PSRAM) soldered to the panel
# driver board — so the size is a property of the board
# board-s3-devkit deliberately STAYS on the 4 MB table even though it is the
# same chip: generic ESP32-S3 devkits ship with 4
# nothing in the image can tell them apart at flash time. Writing this table
# onto a 4 MB module puts ota_1 and both data partitions past the end of
# flash — the app never boots and there is no OTA path back
# recoverable only over serial. A too-small table on a big module merely
# wastes flash. So: 16 MB tables are opt-in per board
# The top 2 MiB (0xE00000..0x1000000) is deliberately left unallocated —
# firmware/build.rs asserts the exact end offset
